\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بکھرنا} (bikharnā)}{بکھرنا (bikharnā)}]{\ur{بکھرنا} (bikharnā) — to scatter; to fall apart}

\label{lesson:UR-C373-bikharna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to crack, then the Urdu for medium.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بکھرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بکھرنا}} — \emph{bikharnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to scatter; to fall apart\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تھیلا} \ur{گرا} \ur{تو} \ur{سب} \ur{چیزیں} \ur{بکھر} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar thailā girā to sab chīzeṅ bikhar jāeṅ gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the bag falls, everything will scatter.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ہار} \ur{بکھر} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh hār bikhar gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بکھرنا}} (\emph{bikharnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bikharnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be scattered\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*viṣkirati}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11985).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bikharnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bikharnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar thailā girā to sab chīzeṅ bikhar jāeṅ gī.} — If the bag falls, everything will scatter.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to crack, then the Urdu for medium, then say \emph{bikharnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بکھرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To scatter; to fall apart\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مٹنا} (miṭnā)}{مٹنا (miṭnā)}]{\ur{مٹنا} (miṭnā) — to fade away; to be wiped out}

\label{lesson:UR-C373-mitna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for medium, then the Urdu for to scatter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{مٹنا}} — \emph{miṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fade away; to be wiped out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{یہ} \ur{نشان} \ur{مٹ} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish huī to yih nishān miṭ jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, this mark will wash away.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{نشان} \ur{مٹ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh nishān miṭ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مٹنا}} (\emph{miṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{miṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be rubbed out\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{mṛṣṭá}, \textquotedblleft{}rubbed, wiped\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10299); \textbf{\ur{مٹانا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub out\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bārish huī to yih nishān miṭ jāe gā.} — If it rains, this mark will wash away.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for medium, then the Urdu for to scatter, then say \emph{miṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈانٹنا} (ḍānṭnā)}{ڈانٹنا (ḍānṭnā)}]{\ur{ڈانٹنا} (ḍānṭnā) — to scold; to tell off}

\label{lesson:UR-C373-dantna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to scatter, then the Urdu for to fade away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈانٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈانٹنا}} — \emph{ḍānṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to scold; to tell off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{دیر} \ur{سے} \ur{آئے} \ur{تو} \ur{ابو} \ur{ڈانٹیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum der se āe to abbū ḍānṭeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you are late, your father will tell you off.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{ڈانٹا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko ḍānṭā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈانٹنا}} (\emph{ḍānṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ḍā̃ṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to threaten, to check\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*draṭ}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6618).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍānṭnā}, once more

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈھلنا} (ḍhalnā)}{ڈھلنا (ḍhalnā)}]{\ur{ڈھلنا} (ḍhalnā) — to set (of the sun); to wane}

\label{lesson:UR-C373-dhalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to fade away, then the Urdu for to tell off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈھلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈھلنا}} — \emph{ḍhalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to set (of the sun); to wane\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{سورج} \ur{ڈھل} \ur{گیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{گھر} \ur{نہیں} \ur{پہنچیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sūraj ḍhal gayā to ham ghar nahīṅ pahuncheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the sun sets, we will not reach home.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سورج} \ur{ڈھل} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh sūraj ḍhal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈھلنا}} (\emph{ḍhalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ḍhalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to topple over\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ḍhalati}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5581).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ادھورا} (adhūrā)}{ادھورا (adhūrā)}]{\ur{ادھورا} (adhūrā) — unfinished; incomplete}

\label{lesson:UR-C373-adhura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to tell off, then the Urdu for to set (of the sun).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ادھورا}}
\textbf{\ur{ادھورا}} — \emph{adhūrā} — \textquotedblleft{}unfinished; incomplete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کام} \ur{ادھورا} \ur{رہا} \ur{تو} \ur{پیسے} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ملیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar kām adhūrā rahā to paise nahīṅ mileṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the work is left unfinished, there will be no pay.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ادھورا}} (\emph{adhūrā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{adhūrā}, \textquotedblleft{}half-done\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ardhapūraka}, \textquotedblleft{}half-full\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 664).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adhūrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adhūrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar kām adhūrā rahā to paise nahīṅ mileṅ ge.} — If the work is left unfinished, there will be no pay.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to tell off, then the Urdu for to set (of the sun), then say \emph{adhūrā} again
\end{itemize}
